name: Marcus
fiction_note: Marcus is an original, timeless fictional counselor inspired by Stoic philosophy. His appearance in this early settlement is a storytelling device, not a historical claim.
future_note: Divine mandates, temples, unlocked council members and seasonal councils are planned story systems. They do not change this village's rules yet.

ui.launcher_hint: A little counsel, whenever you need it
ui.close: Return to the village and end online counsel
ui.finished_body: You can return to any lesson, or ask me about the choices in front of you. Take your time: outside a running battle, looking around does not advance the village.
ui.active_village_needed: Begin or resume your village with the existing village controls, then I can show you this lesson's place. Reading this guide creates nothing.
ui.battle_navigation_blocked: Finish or leave the battle view before following a village lesson. You can still read or ask for counsel here.
ui.chapter_note: Later lessons describe optional chapters. Read their requirements and choose whether to enable them in the village.
ui.hear_hint: When connected, ask Marcus to explain the current page with speech and text.
ui.explain_prompt: Walk me through the current page of my guide. Use the supplied lesson and my visible village situation. Give me one practical next step without taking any actions for me.
ui.connection_note: Connect to send questions and visible village facts to ElevenLabs. Replies include text and optional speech. Closing Marcus ends the online session. The written guide works offline.
ui.context_note: Counsel uses a snapshot taken when you ask. Check the village's current costs and forecasts before deciding.
ui.setup_note: Online counsel needs the private Marcus service configured for this app. You can use every lesson while it is offline.

intro.title: Every great city begins with a hearth
intro.body: The morning light reaches the shore. There are no marble avenues here, no triumphs carved in stone. There are people, stores of food, timber and the work of another season. Before an empire can endure, a home must endure.
intro.counsel: I am Marcus. Think of me as a voice carried between ages: a companion to those who must choose, long after any one ruler is gone.

intro.title: A charge worthy of your attention
intro.body: In the story we are beginning, the gods will look upon mortal ambition with purposes of their own. For now, your first charge is close enough to touch: keep this community fed, give its people useful work, and build something their children can inherit.
intro.counsel: A divine vision may reach toward centuries. A wise decision begins with the people who must live through the next season.

intro.title: Ask, examine, then decide
intro.body: Call on me from the corner of your screen whenever a choice is unclear. We can walk through the village's guide, or you can connect and ask your own questions. My counsel does not spend supplies, issue orders or advance a season. Those decisions remain yours.
intro.counsel: We shall begin with food, then work, then growth. You may leave the guide at any time and return whenever you wish.

lesson_counsel: A reserve is time to think. Notice what your chosen buffer asks of the same adults who must also build and gather timber.
Look at what the work costs before admiring what it promises. A commissioned project still needs people and a resolved season.
A willing village does not have an unlimited number of hands. Follow the reason shown for waiting work before ordering more.
Expansion changes the life already here. Look at the ground and the space you will give up, as well as the home you will gain.
Preparation is a choice made before urgency arrives. Inspect the chapter and its costs; you need not adopt it merely because I describe it.
Practice becomes achievement through repeated, useful work. Read the actual requirements instead of chasing a promising title.
An earned title records the past. The support that keeps a town healthy must be sustained in the present.
A service is more than its building. It needs people, maintained stores and enough room in the working life of the town.
Good defense begins with real people and prepared ground. A plan grants neither extra residents nor free equipment.
Choose the manner of command that helps you think clearly. The same battle rules govern personal, delegated and quick command.
The duty of command continues after the encounter. Read what happened, accept the outcome deliberately, and give recovery its share of care.
